newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CONE STRIKES OUT 16 AS YANKEES BEAT TIGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CONE STRIKES OUT 16 AS YANKEES BEAT TIGERS.

text.p: David Cone struck out a major league season-high 16 over eight innings and finally got some offensive support to carry the New York Yankees to a 5-2 victory over the Detroit Tigers on Monday.

Cone (8-3) allowed two runs and four hits while walking two to improve to 8-1 lifetime against the Tigers. His 147 strikeouts moved him nine ahead of Seattle's Randy Johnson for the major league lead.
Cone had been dominating in his previous two starts but did not get a win either time as his teammates failed to generate any offence for him.
This time former Tiger Cecil Fielder belted a three-run homer in the third and Tino Martinez added his 23rd in the fifth in support of Cone.
"Once Cecil hit the big home run I kind of relaxed," said Cone. "It's the first time I've had a big lead like that in some time.

"I felt like every pitch I had was working," added Cone, who once tied a NL record with 19 strikeouts in one game. "This might have been the best I've thrown ever in terms of being ahead and throwing all my pitches for strikes."
Detroit starter Felipe Lira (4-4) allowed five runs and six hits over seven innings for the loss.
The Tigers got their runs on solo homers by Bob Hamelin in the sixth and Damion Easley in the seventh.
In Milwaukee, Jeff D'Amico threw a four-hitter for his first career shutout and former Oriole Jack Voigt capped a four-run first inning with a two-run double as the Brewers blanked Baltimore 5-0.
D'Amico (5-3) did not walk a batter and struck out six for Milwaukee, which improved to 25-10 at home and returned to .500 for the season at 35-35.
Jeromy Burnitz added a solo homer for the Brewers, who have won five of their last six games.
In Cleveland, Brad Radke posted his fourth successive victory and Pat Meares drove in three runs to pace the Minnesota Twins to a 7-2 victory over the Indians.
Radke (8-5) allowed two runs and six hits over eight innings with a walk and five strikeouts.
Meares's RBI single to centre off starter Chad Ogea (5-8) in the top of the second put the Twins up 3-0. He extended the lead to 5-2 with a two-run homer in the eighth.
Matt Lawton went 4-for-5 and scored twice for the Twins.
Jim Thome supplied all the offence for the Indians with his 19th and 20th homers. Cleveland's Sandy Alomar extended his hitting streak to 22 games with a single in the second.
In Toronto, Wil Cordero, Mike Stanley and Tim Naehring homered in a five-run seventh inning that rallied the Boston Red Sox to a 7-6 victory over the Blue Jays.
Trailing 3-2, Boston broke through against a tiring Woody Williams (2-7). The rally made a winner of Aaron Sele (9-5), who allowed four runs and eight hits in six-plus innings.
Darren Bragg started the rally with an RBI single and Cordero homered for a 5-3 Boston lead. One out later, Stanley and Naehring belted back-to-back solo homers.
The Blue Jays battled back with three runs in the bottom half of the seventh but fell short.

At Texas, Allen Watson scattered six hits over six innings and Jim Leyritz supplied the offence with a homer in the fifth as the Anaheim Angels nipped the Rangers 1-0 for their fifth straight victory.
Watson (6-4) walked one and struck out four before leaving after experiencing tightness in his left shoulder.
Leyritz led off the fifth with a homer off starter Darren Oliver (3-9), who lost despite giving up just one run on six hits in seven innings.
The loss was the sixth in a row for the Rangers, their longest skid in two years.
In Chicago, Chris Snopek's run-scoring groundout in the seventh inning snapped a tie and Albert Belle robbed Chili Davis of a home run in the ninth as the White Sox edged the Kansas City Royals 7-6.
Chicago rallied for three runs in the sixth to knot the contest and Snopek hit a slow bouncer over the mound to score Frank Thomas with the go-ahead run in the seventh.
Davis appeared to have hit a three-run homer in the ninth but Belle extended his glove over the left-field wall and made a game-saving catch.
Matt Karchner won with 1 1/3 scoreless relief innings.

In Seattle, Jay Buhner and Edgar Martinez each drove in a pair of runs as the Mariners jumped out to a five-run lead after two innings and held on for their fifth straight victory, a 6-5 win over the Oakland Athletics.
Oakland starter Dave Telgheder (2-4) was reached for six runs and 11 hits over five innings. Derek Lowe (2-2) pitched five innings for the win, allowing four runs and six hits.
The Athletics got four of their runs on solo homers from Mark Bellhorn, Jason Giambi, Jose Canseco and Matt Stairs.
